interface.title: LasReader (iGEM NCKU-Tainan 2026 · Capture)
interface.field: Synthetic biology / microbiology: quorum-sensing (LasR–AHL) whole-cell biosensor assays, plus swarming-plate phenotyping
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis right after a plate-reader run (standard curve, quantifying unknowns, QC, export). It also has instrument calibration and measurement pages for the team's own reader, and image analysis of agar plates.
interface.what_it_is_for: Fit a weighted 4PL standard curve to AHL biosensor fluorescence standards from one plate, infer each sample's AHL with a 95% CI scaled by its dilution, and export everything, since the tool stores nothing.

data.note: Plate Imaging used the uploaded test file agar-plate-colonies.jpg. In the Plate Reader Assay, the paste box is a plain textarea with no file input, and the browser cannot read plate_fluorescence.txt; uploading it to the Cross-Validation file input only gave a 'missing columns' error (screens/002.webp). So I typed my own 8x12 plate into the textarea. Standards in duplicate rows A–B at 0/1/10/100/1000/10000 nM (2x2 wells each) follow a 4PL with bottom 500, top 50000, EC50 50 nM and Hill 1, and A12 is a deliberate outlier at 21000. Samples are S1 (C1:C3, dilution 10) and S2 (C4:C6, dilution 100). The tool recovered those parameters (screens/025.webp).

features.name: 96-well plate map with range selection and role marking
features.general: Paste a grid of instrument readings, select wells by click, Shift-click range or row/column header, label them as calibrators with a known value or as named unknowns with a dilution, then turn the layout into a replicate table
features.specific: Paste the fluorescence plate; select wells; Mark as Standard (nM) or Sample (name, dilution) or Clear mark; 'N wells marked in M groups'; Fill the table (replaces it)
steps: paste an 8x12 block (the map shows each well's value)
click a well and Shift-click another to select a rectangle (or use a row/column header or All)
choose Mark as Standard and type a concentration, or Sample and type a name and dilution
press 'Mark N wells' (wells marked alike become replicates, at most 6 per group)
press 'Fill the table' to fill the replicate table

Assign each well a role: standard of known concentration, or unknown sample

features.name: Standards table with per-reading residuals and reasoned exclusion

features.specific: Step 2 Standards table: Concentration, n, Mean signal, Mean residual, Reading, Signal, Residual, Exclude checkbox, Reason (required); Fit button
steps: fit and read the residuals (A12 at -16332 stood out)
tick Exclude on the suspect reading (the fit is discarded and Fit is disabled)
type a reason in the Reason box
press Fit again; residuals and n update and the reason is carried into the CSV
serves_tasks: Exclude a questionable reading with a documented reason and refit
Fit a 4-parameter logistic to the standards and read its parameters

features.name: 4PL calibration curve chart with fit summary cards
features.general: Plot calibrator readings (counted vs excluded), mean ± SD and the fitted logistic on a log-x axis with an EC50 marker, show summary metrics, and give a hover tooltip per point
features.specific: Curve chart (Reading counted / excluded, Mean ± SD, 4PL fit, EC50 line) and cards for EC50 with usable range, Hill slope with top/bottom, LOD with LOQ, and RMSE
steps: press Fit
read EC50, Hill slope, LOD/LOQ, RMSE and usable range
hover a point to see its (concentration, signal)
after an exclusion, the excluded point shows as an open circle and the curve and cards update
serves_tasks: Fit a 4-parameter logistic to the standards and read its parameters
Exclude a questionable reading with a documented reason and refit

features.name: Inverse prediction table with CI and dilution scaling
features.general: Back-calculate each unknown's concentration from the fitted curve with a 95% confidence interval, report replicate statistics, multiply by the dilution, and show only the bound for values outside the usable range
features.specific: Step 3 Inferred AHL: Sample, n, Mean signal, SD, CV, AHL in well, 95% CI, Dilution, AHL in sample, 95% CI
steps: fit the curve
read AHL in the well with its 95% CI
read AHL in the sample (× dilution) with its CI
refit after an exclusion and compare how the values and CIs change
serves_tasks: Read each unknown's back-calculated concentration with a 95% CI, corrected for dilution

screens_never_reached: Cross-Validation step 3 'Agreement' (log-log plot, Bland-Altman limits) and step 4 Export: it needs a Plate Reader Assay CSV uploaded in step 1, and the upload tool accepts only the three test files, not files the page downloaded (screens/028.webp). No CAPTURE-Screen batch existed in this browser either.

CAPTURE-Screen Calibrate steps 2–5 (set up, read, fit, save curve): I chose 'Enter recorded data' (screens/004.webp) but did not carry it through within the action budget. The instrument itself is offline (screens/003.webp).
CAPTURE-Screen Curves and Measure: the Measure page says 'No saved curves yet. Calibrate first' (screens/037.webp).
Live spectrum panel and self-check: CAPTURE-Screen is offline, so the Live/LED toggles and Run self-check are disabled (screens/003.webp).
CAPTURE-Screen Data page Export everything (JSON) / Import: disabled because nothing is stored (screens/005.webp).
not_done: Could not use the contents of data/plate_fluorescence.txt: the paste box is a plain textarea, the browser cannot read the file, and the static server returns an error for /data/plate_fluorescence.txt. I typed a synthetic plate following the documented layout instead.
Cross-validating two instruments (log-log plot, Bland-Altman) was blocked at the upload step, as noted above.

Colony measurement on agar-plate-colonies.jpg gave no usable result: the photo shows two hand-held streak plates, the dish circle landed off-centre on the right plate, and 0 colonies were found (screens/032.webp, screens/033.webp). The page has no way to move the circle or outline by hand. Yellow colony outlines and per-colony measurements are therefore unverified.
Did not run a fit in Fluorescence ÷ OD600 mode or with the typed table; I only looked at how the inputs change.
Did not try the table helper buttons (Add standard / Add sample / Add replicate / Remove replicate / Remove row) or Excel-block paste into a table cell.
Did not set an assay type or replicate numbers in Plate Imaging, and did not analyse a batch of several photos.
Did not open the exported curve PNG or annotated plate PNG; they downloaded as binary files.

CAPTURE-Screen Calibrate → Curves → Measure needs a new run through 'Enter recorded data', which needs no hardware; this run stopped at the action budget.
